about: Hand-checkable cases for the point rule. An output on a value three or more outputs share mints 1 point; on a value exactly two share, half a point; alone, none. outputPoints is the sum over all outputs of the transaction; points = the lower of matchedInputs and outputPoints. Values are satoshis.

cases.name: nothing shared
cases.why: Three outputs, all different: no points.

cases.name: one pair
cases.why: Two outputs share a value: half a point each, one point in all. The third is alone.

cases.name: one set of three
cases.why: Three outputs share a value: a full point each.

cases.name: three and a pair
cases.why: A set of three (3 points), a pair (1 point), one alone (0): 4 output points.

cases.name: four of a kind
cases.why: Four outputs share a value: a full point each, 4 output points. Only 2 inputs are matched, so the transaction is worth 2.

cases.name: two pairs
cases.why: Two pairs: one point per pair, 2 output points.

cases.name: inputs are the lower number
cases.why: Six output points but a single matched input: 1 point.

cases.name: outputs are the lower number
cases.why: Nine matched inputs but 4 output points: 4 points.

cases.name: no matched inputs
cases.why: Three output points, no matched input: 0 points.

cases.name: pair turns into three
cases.why: Adding a third output to a pair lifts all three to a full point: 3 output points where the pair had 1.

cases.name: mixed, larger
cases.why: Three sets of three (9), two pairs (2), two alone (0): 11 output points; with 12 matched inputs the transaction is worth 11.
